title: 2016 Preventing in-game Injuries NBA
universal_lens: A Bayesian statistical framework unifying injury risk prediction with player workload and schedule data for real-time tactical decision-making. AUC-based ROC analysis and lift curve validation unify injury prediction models through probabilistic thresholds and strategic rest optimization.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal predictive inference to map player injury probabilities onto probabilistic belief states, enabling dynamic risk-adjusted roster management. Bayesian inference maps predicted injury probabilities to posterior risk distributions; conformal prediction ensures valid uncertainty quantification for player rest decisions.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes state-transition models to simulate player fatigue and injury cascades, supporting adaptive game strategy and rest scheduling decisions. Situational reasoning models player fatigue and game context transitions; state-transition graphs encode risk evolution across 14-day windows for tactical rest scheduling.

primitives.name: Injury Risk Prediction Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this work we present a model that offers a quantitative and systematic approach to injury prevention by allowing teams to predict the likelihood that any given player will succumb to an injury event during the course of an upcoming game.
primitives.assumptions: Players' injury risk is a function of cumulative workload and temporal schedule constraints; model assumes stationary ergodicity of injury processes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P_injury > 0.5, player is classified as high-risk for immediate rest.

layer2.mapping: Maps player-specific workload and schedule data to a probabilistic injury risk kernel via machine learning regression.
layer2.telemetry: Predictive accuracy of injury occurrence within 7-day rolling window

primitives.verbatim_quote: Our model is based on play-­‐by-­‐play game data, SportsVU data, player workload and measurements, and team schedules from the last 2 years.
primitives.assumptions: Workload is additive across game events and inversely correlated with recovery time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When W exceeds threshold W_threshold, risk of acute injury increases exponentially.

primitives.name: Rest Optimization Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: By combining these results with information on team schedules and rest days, our approach enables team management and decision-­‐makers to identify the best time for a team to rest their star players and reduce the risk of long-­‐term injuries, while optimizing team strategies.
primitives.assumptions: Optimal rest is determined by minimizing expected loss of performance due to injury.
primitives.breakdown_regime: R = 1 when P_risk > threshold and T_schedule < buffer period.

layer2.mapping: Derives rest policy from injury risk and schedule constraints using reinforcement-like optimization.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of recommended rest days aligned with actual player usage
